_note: FAKE DATA for the Cauldron TUI — the `prod` environment's seed (other environments: data/soup/<env>.json). Edit freely. Every cluster is a cluster; root clusters play the role of projects. Question `serial` is the permanent per-cluster id (Q-<serial>, spoken 'question <serial>') and must never be reused within its cluster; task `serial` (T-<serial>) and human-action `serial` (HA-<serial>) follow the same rule. `value` (0-100) is the fake ranking signal; blocking questions rank first. Task states: ready | active | done | blocked; `depends_on` lists task serials IN THE SAME CLUSTER. Human-action status: open | resolved | retired. `cauldron` holds the fake dashboards behind the Pools and Mesh tabs and the pools the Settings tab configures (an account's share, enabled switch and note are settings: data/settings/<env>.toml); each mesh device carries the services it runs. `corpus` is the environment's ONE workspace: its schema_version, its regions and its nodes. A task's ripple is its run: active = running, ready/blocked = parked; optional `doing` (what the ripple is doing / waits on) and `account` (where a running one runs) are fake. The `messages` table is FAKE too: invented words in his voice under real-looking ids, standing in for the daemon store a trace will read.

questions.question: When the system is nearly certain what you would say, or your answer would not change what happens next, may it decide and record instead of asking you?
questions.why: This gates everything downstream: how long every cluster's question list is, what the voice reads to you, what may ever interrupt you, and what the dream ripple learns from. It is the single largest lever on your attention.
options: ASK EVERYTHING. Every open question reaches you, only ordered.
CONFIRM, DON'T DECIDE. Near-certain items arrive as 'assumed X, veto?'.
THREE WAYS. Near-certain items are 'assumed, veto?'; inconsequential ones are decided and listed under 'decided for you'; only real forks are asked.
THREE WAYS WITH A FLOOR. As above, but anything touching a directive or constraint you stated is always asked or confirmed.
questions.recommendation: THREE WAYS WITH A FLOOR. Most questions have one obvious answer; recording rather than hiding keeps everything reversible by id, and the floor means nothing you said is quietly overridden.

questions.question: Right after you dump something in, what do you want to hear?
questions.why: This decides the voice ripple's job on the input path and the speed you perceive, since a spoken echo waits for routing and a tone does not. It also decides how fast you catch a misroute.
options: TONE ONLY. A capture tone, then a stored tone.
TONE PLUS ROUTING ECHO. One short line after routing: 'three things: two to Cauldron, one to Broomstick'.
TONE PLUS CHANGES. The echo, plus any new top-ranked item your input created.
questions.recommendation: TONE PLUS ROUTING ECHO, suppressed when every atom stayed in the cluster you are looking at.

questions.question: May Cauldron ever speak to you unprompted, or is everything pull?
questions.why: This sets whether a push path exists at all, and whether a zero-slack blocker can sit unheard for a day.
options: PULL ONLY. Nothing interrupts you.
CRITICAL-PATH PUSH. Only a question blocking the critical path with no slack, at most once per item.
PUSH PLUS DIGEST. Critical-path push, plus a digest when you say 'what's new'.
questions.recommendation: CRITICAL-PATH PUSH, as a tone plus one line you can defer with a word.

questions.question: Are spoken ids 'question forty-one' (type word + per-cluster serial) good enough over speech recognition?
questions.why: Every answer you give by id depends on it; 'fifteen' and 'fifty' are the classic confusion.
options: TYPE WORD + SERIAL, repaired by nearest match among recently spoken ids.
WORD-PAIR IDS like 'amber falcon'.
LIST ORDINALS ('the third one').
questions.recommendation: TYPE WORD + SERIAL. It is your existing scheme made speakable; the audio-position track narrows a misheard number to a handful.

questions.question: May Cauldron discover a relationship between two clusters on its own and carry your input across it?
questions.why: This decides how far the router may reach, and so how often an input lands somewhere you did not expect.
options: DECLARED ONLY. Inputs cross only edges that already exist.
INFERRED AS CONFIRM. The router proposes the edge and applies the atom; both arrive as one 'assumed, veto?' item.
INFERRED FREELY. New relationships are made silently and logged.
questions.recommendation: INFERRED AS CONFIRM. Finding cross-cluster data points is half the value of one input, and one veto reverses both the edge and the write.

regions.handle: THE CLUSTER TREE - how he navigates the cauldron: clusters as nodes, strictly hierarchical, the q:a:p counts, collapse and step-in.
regions.boundary: Inside: how the cluster tree is shaped and walked - parent and child clusters, what a tree row shows, how the arrows and the mouse move through it. Outside: what a cluster REMEMBERS (its regions) goes to R-6's neighbours and the soup; the dump-anything line goes to R-2.

regions.handle: THE DUMP-ANYTHING LINE - one input on every tab, tags that say what he is answering, sends that land on every tagged cluster.
regions.boundary: Inside: the input, the tag grammar ([cluster/Q-1], [region:R-3], [node:IS-12]), the shared draft and the send log. Outside: what a send causes downstream (nothing yet) is not this region's.

regions.handle: RIPPLES - scheduled background work the cauldron runs between his turns: what a ripple is, when it fires, what it may touch.
regions.boundary: Inside: the ripple as a unit of scheduled work, its triggers, its budget and its write scope. Outside: the overnight dream cycle narrows this region (R-4); how a curator folds a turn is R-5's, even when a ripple runs it.

regions.handle: DREAMING - the overnight consolidation ripple: what it reads, what it may rewrite, how its output is reviewed.
regions.boundary: Inside: the dream ripple specifically - its corpus window, its rewrite rights over regions, its morning report. Outside: ripples in general (R-3).

regions.handle: CURATION CRAFT - how a turn is folded into the soup: intake, fold-after, attesting a region by quoting its boundary.
regions.boundary: Inside: the curator's acts and their order, the admission quote, the regionless node and its placement. Outside: the shape of a region itself is the protocol's; scheduled curation runs are R-3's.

regions.handle: ENVIRONMENTS - one cauldron per environment: prod, dev, staging; where each keeps its data and its draft.
regions.boundary: Inside: environment resolution (--env, CAULDRON_ENV, ENV, prod), the data root, what a face may create. Outside: the mesh of devices a cauldron runs across (R-9).

regions.handle: MESH DEVICES - machines joining and leaving the cauldron's mesh, and what each one runs.
regions.boundary: Inside: device membership, heartbeat, which services a device hosts. Outside: environments (R-6); the services themselves are their own repos' business.

regions.handle: LANDING - the public page: copy, pricing, the waitlist form.
regions.boundary: Inside: what a stranger sees before signing up. Outside: the signed-in platform (R-21).

regions.handle: PLATFORM DEPLOY - the signed service, its supervisor, and the quiet-moment restart.
regions.boundary: Inside: building, signing and promoting the platform binary; launchd; is-the-running-process-our-commit. Outside: the landing page (R-20).

regions.handle: THE HARNESS CHAT FACE - the tui that talks to threads: composer, transcript, the mic.
regions.boundary: Inside: the chat face's own behaviour. Outside: the cauldron face built beside it (the cauldron workspace's R-1, R-2).

regions.handle: THE v5 REGIONS PROTOCOL - regions, attestation, caps, and the pen that enforces them.
regions.boundary: Inside: the protocol as written in core:workspaces-v5 and enforced by mind-index-v5. Outside: how one board is migrated (SUB-4 carries the older subject projection that came before it).

regions.handle: SUBJECTS - the v3 subject projection that preceded regions: subject nodes, a capped global tier, expand_on_init.
regions.boundary: Inside: the subjects dogfood as it ran on v3 boards. Outside: v5 regions (R-31). Made under schema v3 and never migrated.

nodes.handle: Globs are Clusters: the tree, the tab and every word in the face say cluster.
nodes.body: Authored by the intake run r-8f3a from 8e4fca10#96: the operator renamed the Globs header to Cluster, and the cauldron tab with it.

nodes.handle: Pools is Energy: the account pools and their threads are one tab, called Energy.
nodes.body: Authored by the intake run r-8f3a from 8e4fca10#96.

nodes.handle: Build the Ripples menu: configure every ripple from the face.
nodes.body: Authored by r-8f3a; made ready by the consequence run r-5b07 when Q-2 closed.

nodes.handle: Is the Ripples menu a cauldron tab or a section of Settings?
nodes.body: Closed by r-8f3a's adjudicate step: a cauldron tab.

nodes.handle: Clusters are nodes and strictly hierarchical; regions map to clusters many-to-many.
nodes.body: His msg 42: clusters are simple and strictly hierarchical, for navigation; a region may be claimed by several clusters, siblings included, and every region should belong to at least one cluster or it becomes undiscoverable.

nodes.handle: A tag hand-typed with a typo is plain text and is never parsed, so the send lands on the focused cluster instead.
nodes.body: Seen in iteration two. The grammar is strict on purpose; the cost is a silent mis-route. A send with an unparsed bracket could be flagged before it is stored.

nodes.handle: Should a send tagged only with a region land on every cluster that claims it?
nodes.body: Built that way in iteration three: a region tag lands on its claimants, a node tag on the claimants of every region it attests. The alternative is the focused cluster only.

nodes.handle: Build the Soup Explorer: every region grouped by workspace, with search.
nodes.body: Iteration three of the cauldron TUI. Search is entered with ^F because printable keys belong to the dump-anything line.

nodes.handle: A ripple that overruns its budget is killed without a record of what it had written.
nodes.body: Observed twice in the trial runs. The ripple's partial writes stay in the soup with no provenance pointing back at the killed run.

nodes.handle: The dream ripple may re-cut a region boundary but never delete a node.
nodes.body: Deletion is his. A re-cut re-quotes every member whose admission span it removes, in the same act.

nodes.handle: Let the dream ripple propose region merges as questions in the morning instead of doing them.
nodes.body: Merges are the riskiest re-cut; asking first costs one question per night.

nodes.handle: Every node attests at least one region, quoting the boundary span that admits it.
nodes.body: The v5 rule (R13, R27). A node no boundary admits is minted regionless and placed in the same round.

nodes.handle: The draft typed in a not-yet-existing environment silently created that environment.
nodes.body: Resolved by making the environments menu say so: a seeded environment is created on its first draft write.

nodes.handle: A second device joins the mesh and shows its load on the Mesh tab.
nodes.body: Today the mesh is one machine. Nobody has claimed this region yet, so no cluster in the Surface sidebar reaches it.

nodes.handle: Does pricing show per-seat or per-workspace on the landing page?
nodes.body: Two drafts exist. Per-seat reads cheaper; per-workspace matches how the product is used.

nodes.handle: An agent never restarts a supervised service; the quiet-moment absorb path decides.
nodes.body: Standing prohibition, cited from the signed-service doctrine.

nodes.handle: The promote tool leaves its scratch directory behind when codesign fails.
nodes.body: The cleanup runs only on the success path. Seen once on 2026-10-02.

nodes.handle: The chat face moved into the cauldron repo; `cauldron tui --chat` opens it.
nodes.body: The bare `cauldron tui` opens the cauldron face; the chat face keeps its own binary name `tui`.

nodes.handle: Every cap is HARD by one character; the remedy is a carve, never a trim.
nodes.body: From the v5 protocol. Measured, cap and overage are printed on every refusal.

nodes.handle: The subject projection still renders on two boards that never migrated to v5.
nodes.body: SUB-4 is the record of it. Those boards show schema v3 regions beside v5 ones.
